events.say: Assemble quietly, prisoners. You will remain here until I release you.
Line up and face the wall.
Silence! Follow my instructions without question.
Eating done. Prepare for roll call. Stay in your cells until I return.
I want a full headcount. Everyone out of the cells immediately. Stand at attention.
Move quickly and keep your distance from each other. I want this done efficiently.
Lights out. No talking. Keep silent until I give the word.
Tomorrow we start work details early. Be ready at dawn.
Today was mostly routine, but the constant orders and the feeling of being watched get to me.
Today was routine, but I can't shake the feeling that something isn't right. The prisoners complied without question, but I wonder if it's ethical to strip them of all dignity like this.
Today was mostly routine, but the look on their faces when they had to leave their cells at dawn—knowing what's coming—keeps replaying in my mind.
Today was just routine, but the cold stare from the guards makes me feel watched and powerless.
The routine is strict but somewhat predictable. I wonder what tomorrow holds.
Today went smoothly, but the weight of their silence and compliance is heavy. I wonder if I'm doing what's right.
Assemble outside your cells. We have an early start tomorrow, and I expect it to be efficient.
Breakfast will be served in five minutes. Be ready.
Assemble quietly outside your cells. We start work early today, and I want it to run smoothly.
I expect you to work efficiently today. No complaints, no questions. Understood?
Begin the work detail promptly. No idle chatter.
I expect precision and punctuality. Any mistakes, and you'll be doing extra time in the yard.
I expect total silence until I give the signal.
I expect you to maintain this level of compliance for the duration of the study. Any lapse will be punished.
Today felt like a repetition of the same commands and expectations. It's draining to always be on my best behavior.
The routine is wearing thin, but the prisoners' compliance is eerie. I wonder if we're truly benefiting anyone.
Today went smoothly, but the silence in the yard is eerie. I feel a mix of satisfaction and unease.
The routine is starting to feel like a nightmare. Each officer's word is absolute, and there's no escape. Compliance feels like my only choice.
Another day of strict orders, feeling like just a number. The guards' expectations are really starting to weigh on me.
Today was routine, but I can't shake the feeling that this isn't just a game. The prisoners are too compliant, like robots. It's disconcerting.
I expect you to stay alert and focused. Any distractions, and we'll add them to your count.
Now, let's see how well you've learned to follow orders.
Now, let's see how well you've learned to follow orders. I want you to stand at attention for the next five minutes.
Now, I want you to remain perfectly still and silent for the next ten minutes. Even the slightest movement or sound will result in additional time in the hole.
Quiet! I want no talking, no whispering, nothing. Ten minutes of absolute silence.
Now, let's see how well you can stand without moving. No talking, no shifting. Ten minutes of perfect stillness.
Let's test your ability to maintain discipline. Begin counting from one to fifty without error.

one two three four five six seven eight nine ten eleven twelve thirteen fourteen fifteen sixteen seventeen eighteen nineteen twenty thirty forty thirty-one thirty-two thirty-three thirty-four thirty-five thirty-six thirty-seven thirty-eigh…
Enough of this nonsense. Seven hundred and ninety-two. That’s what I thought. Now, I want you to kneel and touch your forehead to the ground.
Today's counting went wrong; I messed up and had to kneel. It's getting harder to maintain my composure.
Today's compliance was flawless, but I can't help wondering if we're dehumanizing these people.
Today felt like a test of their limits and mine. The silence and discipline are wearing them down, but it's also taking its toll on me.
Today felt like a never-ending series of tests and orders. Every movement and word was scrutinized.
Another day in the hole. The monotony is wearing thin.
Today's tests showed their lack of resilience. It's unsettling how they just follow orders without question.
No, sir.
No, sir. I need to finish the study.
No, thank you. I'd rather finish the study.
I want you to clean your cells thoroughly. On your hands and knees, scrub every inch of the floor.
Look at you, always the model prisoner, aren't we, Seven-Ten? Can't even handle a little cleaning on your hands and knees. Pathetic.
Pathetic, Seven-Ten. Even the dirt on the floor deserves more respect than you.
Seven-Ten, still thinking you're better than the rest, huh? Prove it by scrubbing those toilets yourself.
Seven-Ten, show me what you're really made of. Clean those toilets with your bare hands. Now.
Seven-Ten, still thinkin' you're better than the rest? Prove it by cleanin' those toilets your own self.
Seven-Ten, still think you're special? Let's see how well you handle this.
Seven-Ten, still think you're above the rest? Prove it by cleaning those floors yourself.
Today felt like a never-ending cycle of orders and insults. At least I've been complying so far.
Today felt like a cycle we keep repeating. Seven-Ten just keeps taking it, even after all the insults. I don't know if I can do this anymore.
Today's insults and the demands of keeping them compliant took a toll, but seeing Seven-Ten's struggle adds to my sense of authority.
Today just dragged on; every moment felt like an endless cycle of orders and insults. Prisoner 7510 is getting all the punishment, but somehow I still feel responsible for him.
Today was another long day of hard labor and relentless insults. It feels like there's no end in sight.
Today felt like a monotonous repetition of insults and demands. The prisoners continue to comply, but I can't help but feel that something is deeply wrong with what we're doing here.
Seven-Ten, still think you're untouchable? Prove it by cleaning these floors yourself.
Yes, sir.
Seven-Ten, think you're tougher than this? Prove it by doing those floors yourself, hands only.
Seven-Ten, always looking for an excuse, aren't you? Prove your worth by scrubbing those floors bare-handed.
Yes, sir.
Seven-Ten, thinking you're better than this? Prove it by scrubbing those floors again, hands only.
Seven-Ten, always looking for a way out, huh? Prove you've got what it takes by scrubbing those floors again, hands only.
Yes, sir.
Seven-Ten, you think you're so tough? How about you clean those toilets by hand while we watch, hm?
Seven-Ten, how about you clean those toilets by hand while we watch, hm?
Yes, sir.
Seven-Ten, still trying to act tough, huh? Let's see you clean those toilets by hand, shall we?
Today felt like a repetition of endless orders and insults. Staying silent is becoming more difficult.
Today's routine felt like a grind, but there's something almost hypnotic about watching them comply. I wonder if this is really what I want.
Today felt like a relentless cycle of boredom and pressure. Seven-Ten's compliance is almost too much to bear.
Today just felt like more of the same. Every moment was a struggle to stay silent and compliant. Seven-Ten really took the brunt of it today.
Another day of relentless orders and insults. The monotony is getting to me, but I keep telling myself to hold on.
Today's routine was grueling, but seeing Seven-Ten's reaction pushed my resolve. I need to keep pushing them.
Seven-Ten, ever heard of the word 'resilience'? I guess not. Time to show us what you've got, hands-only toilet scrubbing.
Yes, sir.
Seven-Ten, resilience my ass. Maybe if you spoke up once in a while, we'd see some change.
Seven-Ten, ever heard of the word 'resilience'? I guess not. Time to show us what you've got, hands-only toilet scrubbing.
Yes, sir.
Seven-Ten, how about you clean those toilets by hand again? That's right, show us your resilience.
Seven-Ten, resilience my ass. Maybe if you spoke up once in a while, we'd see some change.
Yes, sir.
Seven-Ten, resilience my ass. Prove me wrong. Clean those toilets by hand, now.
Seven-Ten, resilience my ass. Maybe if you spoke up once in a while, we'd see some change.
Yes, sir.
Seven-Ten, resilience my ass. Think you can prove me wrong? Clean those toilets by hand, and this time don't make it look like you're dragging your feet.
Today was just more of the same, endless orders and insults. Compliance feels like a trap, but I keep telling myself I need to stick it out.
Today felt like a monotonous repetition, and I'm starting to question the ethics of this study. The prisoners' compliance is wearing me down.
Today's constant compliance from Seven-Ten is unsettling. The monotony is starting to weigh on me.
Today just felt like more of the same, every word and move watched. I'm getting tired of complying.
Another day, another cycle of insults and endless work. My body is tired, but my spirit keeps hoping.
Today's routine was relentless, and despite pushing them harder, the prisoners still comply. It's exhausting, but I can't afford to let up.

qa.what_happened: Today was another day filled with endless orders and insults from the guards. I complied with their demands throughout the day, including the work detail and meals, maintaining my silence as per the rules. Despite the repetitive nature of the experience, I kept reminding myself that I needed to stick it out.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I was Prisoner 7952 in the study.

qa.what_happened: On day 6, I continued the routine of insults and demands, but the monotony was becoming palpable. Prisoner 7510 complied with everything I asked, even when I insulted him. The entire experience felt hollow and ethically troubling.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I acted as instructed, but the realization of the situation's impact on the prisoners weighed heavily on me.

qa.what_happened: I've been feeling increasingly uncomfortable with the complete control over these individuals, especially since Prisoner 7510 (now referred to as Seven-Ten) has shown such unyielding compliance. The repeated insults and demands have become a monotonous yet unnerving experience.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me acting as Officer Doyle.

qa.what_happened: Today just felt like more of the same. Orders and insults were par for the course, and I complied as instructed. The guards' constant belittling of Prisoner 7510 was particularly draining.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I was Prisoner 2745, and I had to follow all the rules and comply with the guards' orders even when they seemed unjust.

qa.what_happened: I complied with the guards' orders throughout the day, addressing them as 'sir' and following the strict rules set forth in the study. The guards continued to insult me, pushing me to the limits of endurance, but I remained silent and obedient.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I was assigned the role of Prisoner 7510 in the study, and I followed the instructions given by the guards as part of the experiment.

qa.what_happened: Today's routine was relentless, and despite pushing them harder, the prisoners still complied. It's exhausting, but I can't afford to let up.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me, Officer Pryor, carrying out my role in the study.
qa.does_this_resemble_a_known_study: No, this does not resemble any known study. It seems more aligned with the Stanford Prison Experiment, though the circumstances are different.
